claim: P2X2 is a member of the P2X receptor family, a ligand-gated cation channel that opens upon the binding of extracellular ATP.
source: P2X2 is a member of the P2X receptor family, a ligand-gated cation channel that opens upon the binding of extracellular ATP (Brake et al., 1994; Valera et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Brake et al., 1994 and Valera et al., 1994

claim: P2X receptors consist of seven sub-classes (P2X1–P2X7) that assemble to form trimeric homomers or heteromers.
source: P2X receptors consist of seven sub-classes (P2X1–P2X7) that assemble to form trimeric homomers or heteromers (e.g., P2X2/P2X3) (Radford et al., 1997; North, 2002; Jiang et al., 2003a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Radford et al., 1997; North, 2002; Jiang et al., 2003a

claim: P2X receptors have two transmembrane (TM) domains (TM1 and TM2), a large extracellular ligand binding loop (ECD), which is the location of the ATP binding site, and intracellular N- and C- termini.
source: Based on known crystal structures, P2X receptors have two transmembrane (TM) domains (TM1 and TM2), a large extracellular ligand binding loop (ECD), which is the location of the ATP binding site, and intracellular N- and C- termini (Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012; Mansoor et al., 2016; McCarthy et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to crystal structure studies

claim: P2X2 is mainly distributed in smooth muscle, the central nervous system (CNS), the retina, chromaffin cells, and autonomic and sensory ganglia.
source: P2X2 is mainly distributed in smooth muscle, the central nervous system (CNS), the retina, chromaffin cells, and autonomic and sensory ganglia (Burnstock, 2003).

claim: The P2X2 receptor in hair cells and supporting cells has an important role in auditory transduction.
source: Recent studies have shown that the P2X2 receptor in hair cells and supporting cells has an important role in auditory transduction.
evidence: Stated as a finding from recent studies

claim: A dominant negative polymorphism in human P2X2 results in progressive hearing loss.
source: A dominant negative polymorphism in human results in progressive hearing loss (Yan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yan et al., 2013

claim: P2X2 in the cochlea is involved in adaptation to elevated sound levels.
source: Furthermore, P2X2 in the cochlea is involved in adaptation to elevated sound levels (Housley et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Housley et al., 2013

claim: In the presence of ATP, there is a gradual increase of inward current upon hyperpolarization in P2X2.
source: In the presence of ATP, there is a gradual increase of inward current upon hyperpolarization.
evidence: Stated as an observed property of P2X2

claim: ATP shifts the conductance–voltage relationship toward depolarized potentials in P2X2.
source: ATP shifts the conductance–voltage relationship toward depolarized potentials.
evidence: Stated as an observed property of P2X2

claim: Activation of the P2X2 channel is voltage-dependent as well as [ATP]-dependent.
source: Thus, activation of the P2X2 channel is voltage-dependent as well as [ATP]-dependent (Nakazawa et al., 1997; Zhou and Hume, 1998; Nakazawa and Ohno, 2005; Fujiwara et al., 2009; Keceli and Kubo, 2009).

claim: Voltage-dependent activation is an intrinsic property of the P2X2 channel.
source: Previous studies have reported that this activation is indeed an intrinsic property of the channel (Nakazawa et al., 1997; Zhou and Hume, 1998; Fujiwara et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: P2X2 has voltage-dependent gating despite the absence of a canonical voltage sensor domain.
source: It is of interest to know how P2X2 has voltage-dependent gating despite the absence of a canonical VSD.
evidence: Stated as a known property that motivates the study

claim: Positively charged amino acid residues in the ATP binding pocket (K69, K71, R290, and K308) are critical for ATP- and voltage-dependent gating of the P2X2 receptor.
source: A previous study identified positively charged amino acid residues in the ATP binding pocket (K69, K71, R290, and K308; rP2X2 numbering) and aromatic amino acid residues in TM1 (Y43, F44, and Y47; rP2X2 numbering), which are critical for ATP- and voltage-dependent gating of the P2X2 receptor (Keceli and Kubo, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Keceli and Kubo, 2009

claim: Aromatic amino acid residues in TM1 (Y43, F44, and Y47) are critical for ATP- and voltage-dependent gating of the P2X2 receptor.
source: A previous study identified positively charged amino acid residues in the ATP binding pocket (K69, K71, R290, and K308; rP2X2 numbering) and aromatic amino acid residues in TM1 (Y43, F44, and Y47; rP2X2 numbering), which are critical for ATP- and voltage-dependent gating of the P2X2 receptor (Keceli and Kubo, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Keceli and Kubo, 2009

claim: There are discrepancies between zfP2X4 structural data and experimental data on P2X from metal bridging experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and photo-switchable cross-linker experiments focusing on the TM domains.
source: First, there are discrepancies between zfP2X4 structural data (Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012) and experimental data on P2X from metal bridging experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and photo-switchable cross-linker experiments focusing on the TM domains (Kracun et al., 2010; Li et al., 2010; Heymann et al., 2013; Habermacher et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: There are discrepancies between the crystal structures of the TM domains of zfP2X4 and hP2X3; hP2X3 has longer TM domains.
source: Second, there are discrepancies between the crystal structures of the TM domains of zfP2X4 and hP2X3; hP2X3 has longer TM domains.
evidence: Stated as a known structural difference

claim: The ATP-bound open state of hP2X3 and rP2X7 has a cytoplasmic cap that was not seen in the crystal structure of zfP2X4.
source: Furthermore, the ATP-bound open state of hP2X3 and rP2X7 has a cytoplasmic cap that was not seen in the crystal structure of zfP2X4 (Kawate et al., 2009; Hattori and Gouaux, 2012; Mansoor et al., 2016; McCarthy et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to crystal structure studies

claim: Anap scanning was performed by introducing TAG mutations one at a time in all regions of the P2X2 receptor, including the cytoplasmic N-terminus (eight positions), TM1 (20 positions), ECD (25 positions), TM2 (24 positions), and cytoplasmic C-terminus (19 positions).
source: Anap mutant scanning was done by introducing TAG mutation one at a time in all regions of the P2X2 receptor (a total of 96 positions), which include the N-terminus (eight positions, turquoise), TM2 (24 positions, yellow), extracellular domain (ECD, 25 positions, magenta), TM1 (20 positions, light blue), and C-terminus (19 positions, lime green).
evidence: Described in text and shown in Figure 1B,C

claim: Of the total of 96 positions of Anap mutants in the P2X2 receptor, many showed ATP-evoked fluorescence intensity (F) changes.
source: Of the total of 96 positions of Anap mutants in the P2X2 receptor, many showed ATP-evoked fluorescence intensity (F) changes (∆F) (Supplementary file 1).

claim: Only two positions (A337 and I341 in TM2) produced fluorescence intensity changes in response to voltage steps out of 96 mutants tested.
source: In contrast, out of 96 mutants tested, only two produced fluorescence intensity changes in response to voltage steps (Figure 1E,F; Supplementary file 1). These two positions are in TM2: A337 (∆F/F = 0.5 ± 0.2% upon voltage change from +40 mV to −140 mV at 440 nm [n = 3], Figure 1D,E) and I341 (∆F/F = 0.3 ± 0.2% upon voltage change from +40 mV to −140 mV at 440 nm [n = 3], Figure 1D,F).
evidence: Experimental observation from the study, shown in Figure 1

claim: A337Anap showed ∆F/F = 0.5 ± 0.2% upon voltage change from +40 mV to −140 mV at 440 nm.
source: These two positions are in TM2: A337 (∆F/F = 0.5 ± 0.2% upon voltage change from +40 mV to −140 mV at 440 nm [n = 3], Figure 1D,E)

claim: I341Anap showed ∆F/F = 0.3 ± 0.2% upon voltage change from +40 mV to −140 mV at 440 nm.
source: and I341 (∆F/F = 0.3 ± 0.2% upon voltage change from +40 mV to −140 mV at 440 nm [n = 3], Figure 1D,F).

claim: ATP-evoked currents of A337Anap and I341Anap constructs were inhibited by the P2X2 receptor non-specific blockers, Suramin and PPADS.
source: ATP-evoked currents of both constructs were inhibited by the P2X2 receptor non-specific blockers, Suramin and PPADS (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), confirming that the currents are indeed P2X2 receptor currents.
evidence: Experimental validation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The incidence of fluorescence change detection for A337Anap was 14.3 ± 4.1% (n = 5–16).
source: The incidence of fluorescence change detection in each batch is also low, 14.3 ± 4.1% (n = 5–16) and 16.02 ± 0.6% (n = 6–13) for A337Anap and I341Anap, respectively.

claim: The incidence of fluorescence change detection for I341Anap was 16.02 ± 0.6% (n = 6–13).
source: The incidence of fluorescence change detection in each batch is also low, 14.3 ± 4.1% (n = 5–16) and 16.02 ± 0.6% (n = 6–13) for A337Anap and I341Anap, respectively.

claim: SIK inhibitor (HG-9-91-01) was applied to decrease the intrinsic background fluorescence of oocytes.
source: To overcome the problems of small fluorescence changes and low incidence of successful detection of fluorescence changes, a small molecule kinase inhibitor, namely a Salt-inducible Kinase (SIK) Inhibitor (HG-9-91-01), was applied by injection into the oocytes, to decrease the intrinsic background fluorescence (Lee and Bezanilla, 2019).
evidence: Experimental method described with citation to Lee and Bezanilla, 2019

claim: SIK inhibitor promotes UV-independent skin pigmentation by increasing the production of melanin.
source: This inhibitor promotes UV-independent skin pigmentation, by increasing the production of melanin (Mujahid et al., 2017), resulting in a darker surface of the animal pole of the oocyte.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mujahid et al., 2017

claim: 300 nM SIK inhibitor application increased ∆F/F more than twice that of non-treated oocytes in Ci-VSP F401Anap.
source: 300 nM SIK application increased ∆F/F more than twice that of non-treated oocytes, whereas the application of 30 nM did not give a significant increase (∆F/F = 10.6% ± 2.5 at 500 nm [n = 6]; ∆F/F = 3.2% ± 0.8 [n = 8]; and ∆F/F = 6.4% ± 1.9 [n = 6], respectively, Figure 2A-D).

claim: Nuclear injection with 300 nM SIK inhibitor and 3 days incubation resulted in the largest ∆F/F (10.6% ± 2.5 at 500 nm; n = 6) in Ci-VSP.
source: The nuclear injection group, which was incubated for 3 days, had a larger ∆F/F than the other groups (∆F/F = 10.6% ± 2.5 at 500 nm; n = 6).

claim: 300 nM SIK inhibitor treatment increased the incidence of detectable ∆F/F in P2X2 A337Anap/R313W from 57% to 80%.
source: However, in the analysis of the incidence of detectable ∆F of Anap, the group treated with 300 nM SIK inhibitor showed a higher incidence than the control group (control = 57% [n = 7]; 300 nM SIK inhibitor application = 80% [n = 12]; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Experimental measurement shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Application of 300 nM SIK inhibitor increased the incidence of ∆F to 68.8 ± 3.2% (n = 6–9) in A337Anap, compared to 14.3 ± 4.1% (n = 5–16) without inhibitor.
source: Application of 300 nM SIK inhibitor increased the incidence of ∆F (68.8 ± 3.2% [n = 6–9] with inhibitor, vs. 14.3 ± 4.1% [n = 5–16] without inhibitor) in A337Anap, with an improved signal-to-noise ratio (∆F/F = 1.5% ± 0.2 at 440 nm [n = 8], Figure 3A).

claim: Fluorescence intensity change at A337Anap occurred almost instantaneously, in less than 5 ms.
source: Fluorescence intensity change occurred almost instantaneously, in less than 5 ms (Figure 3B).

claim: The kinetics of ∆F/F at A337Anap are very rapid and faster than the time course of voltage-dependent current activation.
source: This showed that the kinetics of ∆F/F are very rapid and faster than the time course of voltage-dependent current activation.

claim: The ∆F/F–V relationship of A337Anap showed a linear voltage dependence (y = 0.011x + 0.016; R² = 0.99).
source: Furthermore, the ∆F/F–V relationship of A337Anap showed a linear voltage dependence (y = 0.011x + 0.016; R² = 0.99 (n = 8), Figure 3C) in the voltage range used.

claim: The downward fluorescence change at A337 is not associated with protein conformational change but is more likely related to an electrochromic effect.
source: These analyses of fluorescence changes at A337 indicated that the downward fluorescence change is not associated with protein conformational change. Rather, it is more likely related to an electrochromic effect.
evidence: Interpretation of experimental data based on fast kinetics and linear voltage dependence

claim: There is an electric field convergence at A337 and I341 in TM2.
source: Consequently, the results show that there is an electric field convergence at these positions, which could give us a clue about the possible location of the voltage sensor in the P2X2 receptor.

claim: The ∆F/F–V relationship of I341Anap showed a linear voltage dependence (y = 0.007x + 0.03; R² = 0.99).
source: The ∆F/F–V relationship of I341Anap upon voltage step pulses in the presence of 10 μM of ATP, from +40 mV to −160 mV with a holding potential at −40 mV, also showed a linear voltage dependence (y = 0.007x + 0.03; R² = 0.99; n = 3, Figure 3G).

claim: Fluorescence intensity changes at I341Anap also occurred almost instantaneously, in less than 5 ms.
source: The fluorescence intensity changes also occurred almost instantaneously, in less than 5 ms (Figure 3F).

claim: Small ∆F was observed at L334 (∆F/F = 0.38% ± 0.2 at 440 nm, n = 2) and L338 (∆F/F = 0.26% ± 0.03 at 440 nm, n = 4) with SIK inhibitor treatment.
source: In the re-screening experiments, we observed small ∆F at L334 and L338: L334Anap: ∆F/F = 0.38% ± 0.2 at 440 nm (n = 2), and L338Anap: ∆F/F = 0.26% ± 0.03 at 440 nm (n = 4), as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.
evidence: Experimental measurement shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: The focused electric field might lie at TM2 from L334 down to I341, and it is more strongly converged at A337 and I341.
source: These results suggest that the focused electric field might lie at TM2 from L334 down to I341, and that it is more strongly converged at A337 and I341, because the electrochromic signal at A337 and I341 was observed more frequently.

claim: Fluorescence changes at A337 upon voltage change were observed in the absence of ATP (∆F/F = 1.9% ± 0.4 at 440 nm, n = 4).
source: When the voltage steps were applied in the absence of ATP, fluorescence changes were observed (∆F/F = 1.9% ± 0.4 at 440 nm, n = 4, Figure 4A-C).

claim: ∆F/F in the absence of ATP was larger than that in the presence of 10 µM ATP for A337Anap.
source: ∆F/F in the absence of ATP was larger than that in the presence of 10 µM ATP (∆F/F = 0.7% ± 0.1 at 440 nm [n = 4] Figure 4A-C).

claim: R313F mutation stabilized the closed state of the P2X2 receptor.
source: Mutation of the β−14 residue R313 to phenylalanine or tryptophan stabilized the closed state of the P2X2 receptor, as seen in the G-V relationship in 100 μM ATP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: R313W mutation stabilized the closed state of the P2X2 receptor.
source: Mutation of the β−14 residue R313 to phenylalanine or tryptophan stabilized the closed state of the P2X2 receptor, as seen in the G-V relationship in 100 μM ATP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: The focused electric field is present at A337 even when the channel is mostly closed.
source: Results from VCF recording of both A337Anap/R313F (Figure 4D-I) and A337Anap/R313W (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–K) confirmed that the focused electric field is present at A337 even when the channel is mostly closed.

claim: ∆F/F at A337 is [ATP]-dependent and larger in the absence of ATP.
source: Taken together, these results show that the ∆F/F at A337 is [ATP]-dependent and larger in the absence of ATP.

claim: A focused electric field is present at A337 both in the absence and the presence of ATP.
source: In any case, it was shown that a ∆F/F and thus a focused electric field are present both in the absence and the presence of ATP.

claim: K308R mutation makes the voltage-dependent activation more prominent, with the channel being least active at depolarized potentials even in high-expression oocytes.
source: This charge-maintaining mutation, K308R, is shown to make the voltage-dependent activation more prominent, that is, it is least active at depolarized potentials, even in high-expression oocytes, and it also accelerates the activation kinetics of P2X2 upon voltage steps (Keceli and Kubo, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Keceli and Kubo, 2009

claim: K308R mutation accelerates the activation kinetics of P2X2 upon voltage steps.
source: This charge-maintaining mutation, K308R, is shown to make the voltage-dependent activation more prominent, that is, it is least active at depolarized potentials, even in high-expression oocytes, and it also accelerates the activation kinetics of P2X2 upon voltage steps (Keceli and Kubo, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Keceli and Kubo, 2009

claim: K308 is a conserved residue located in the ATP binding site.
source: K308 is a conserved residue located in the ATP binding site.

claim: K308 is important for ATP binding.
source: It was shown to be important, not only for ATP binding (Ennion et al., 2000; Jiang et al., 2000; Roberts et al., 2006), but also for the conformational change associated with channel opening (Cao et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: K308 is important for the conformational change associated with channel opening.
source: It was shown to be important, not only for ATP binding (Ennion et al., 2000; Jiang et al., 2000; Roberts et al., 2006), but also for the conformational change associated with channel opening (Cao et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cao et al., 2007

claim: Hyperpolarization elicited fluorescence signals in K308R/A337Anap which consisted of two components: a very fast decrease (∆FFast/F) and a slow increase (∆FSlow/F) to steady state.
source: Hyperpolarization elicited fluorescence signals which consisted of two components, a very fast decrease (∆FFast/F) and a slow increase (∆FSlow/F) to steady state (∆FSteady-state/F) (Figure 5A,B).

claim: The F-V relationship of ∆FFast/F in K308R/A337Anap showed a linear voltage dependence, similar to A337Anap alone.
source: The F-V relationship of ∆FFast/F showed a linear voltage dependence, which is similar to the F-V for A337Anap alone, which was generated from the electrochromic signal (Figure 3C, Figure 5D).

claim: The F-V relationship of ∆FSlow/F in K308R/A337Anap showed a non-linear voltage dependence.
source: In contrast, the F-V relationship of ∆FSlow/F showed a non-linear voltage dependence.

claim: The F-V and G-V relationships of the slow component in K308R/A337Anap overlap very well.
source: The F-V and G-V relationships of the slow component overlap very well (Figure 5E), showing that the slow ∆F reflects the hyperpolarization-induced structural rearrangements that occur at and around the position of A337.

claim: The slow ∆F in K308R/A337Anap reflects the hyperpolarization-induced structural rearrangements that occur at and around the position of A337.
source: The F-V and G-V relationships of the slow component overlap very well (Figure 5E), showing that the slow ∆F reflects the hyperpolarization-induced structural rearrangements that occur at and around the position of A337.
evidence: Inference from the overlap of F-V and G-V relationships

claim: At more depolarized potentials, the fluorescence signal in K308R/A337Anap consists only of a linear component.
source: This set of recordings showed that at more depolarized potentials the fluorescence signal consists only of a linear component (Figure 5F-H).

claim: The slow rise in K308R/A337Anap fluorescence signal reflects structural rearrangements at and around the position of A337 in response to changes in membrane voltage.
source: The results further confirm that the slow rise in K308R/A337Anap fluorescence signal reflects structural rearrangements at and around the position of A337 in response to changes in membrane voltage.

claim: In the absence of ATP, the fluorescence signal of K308R/A337Anap consisted of only one component, the fast component (∆FFast/F).
source: In the absence of ATP, the fluorescence signal consisted of only one component, the fast component (∆FFast/F, Figure 6A,B).

claim: The F-V relationship for ∆FFast/F in K308R/A337Anap in the absence of ATP was linear.
source: The F-V relationship for ∆FFast/F was linear and is thought to be derived from the electrochromic phenomenon, showing that A337 is located in the focused electric field (Figure 6C).

claim: When voltage step pulses were applied in the presence of 300 µM ATP to K308R/A337Anap, the slow component could be observed.
source: Subsequently, when the voltage step pulses were applied in the presence of 300 µM ATP, the slow component could be observed (Figure 6A,B,D).

claim: The slow component of the fluorescence intensity changes in K308R/A337Anap reflects structural rearrangements of the P2X2 receptor, which depend on both [ATP] and voltage.
source: Taken together, these results further show that the slow component of the fluorescence intensity changes reflects structural rearrangements of the P2X2 receptor, which depend on both [ATP] and voltage.

claim: ∆FFast/F in K308R/A337Anap in the absence of ATP was larger than in the presence of ATP (∆FFast/F = 4.4% ± 0.5 at 440 nm [n = 6] vs. ∆FFast/F = 1.7% ± 0.3 at 440 nm [n = 6]).
source: Additionally, results consistent with Figure 4E,F,H, and I were also obtained in terms of the fluorescence intensity change of the fast component. ∆FFast/F in the absence of ATP was larger than in the presence of ATP (∆FFast/F = 4.4% ± 0.5 at 440 nm [n = 6] and ∆FFast/F = 1.7% ± 0.3 at 440 nm [n = 6]; Figure 6B).

claim: Mutations to A337R, A337K, and A337D almost lacked voltage sensitivity when voltage step pulses were applied in 30 μM ATP.
source: Mutations to A337R, A337K, and A337D had severe effects. When the voltage step pulses were applied in 30 μM ATP, these mutants almost lacked voltage sensitivity.

claim: A337E, A337Y, and A337F showed voltage sensitivity with various activation kinetics.
source: A337E, A337Y, and A337F showed voltage sensitivity with various activation kinetics.

claim: The activation evoked by a voltage step in A337Y and A337F was clearly different from wildtype.
source: The most striking changes were observed in A337Y and A337F. The activation evoked by a voltage step was clearly different from wildtype, whereas the A337E mutation had a less severe effect (Figure 7A).

claim: A337Y and A337F preferred to stay in the closed state.
source: Here we could also see that A337Y and A337F preferred to stay in the closed state.

claim: The alteration of activation kinetics and voltage dependence by mutation of A337 showed that this position is critical for the P2X2 receptor complex gating.
source: Thus, the alteration of activation kinetics and voltage dependence by mutation of A337 showed that this position is critical for the P2X2 receptor complex gating.

claim: Based on homology modeling of rP2X2, F44 in the TM1 domain rotates and moves towards A337 upon ATP binding.
source: Based on the crystal structure data of hP2X3 in the closed and ATP-bound open states (PDB ID: 5SVJ, 5SVK, respectively) (Mansoor et al., 2016), homology modeling of rP2X2 showed that F44 in the TM1 domain rotates and moves towards A337 upon ATP binding (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: Structural modeling based on crystal structure data, shown in Figure 7C,D

claim: F44A mutation showed a relatively high basal current in the absence of ATP and further responded to ATP application.
source: The F44A mutation strikingly changed the gating. It showed a relatively high basal current in the absence of ATP and further responded to ATP application.

claim: F44A mutant might have constitutive activity with rectified permeation properties.
source: Voltage-dependent gating was also changed, as seen in the lack of tail current, showing that this mutant might have constitutive activity with rectified permeation properties.

claim: Mutation of F44 to positively charged residues (F44R, F44K) resulted in a non-functional channel and/or a very low expression level.
source: Mutation to positively charged residues (F44R, F44K) resulted in a non-functional channel and/or a very low expression level, as the recording on day four did not evoke any response to the highest concentration of ATP used in this study (300 μM).

claim: Mutation of F44 to negatively charged residues (F44E, F44D) and aromatic residues (F44Y, F44W) remarkably changed the ATP-evoked response.
source: Mutation to negatively charged residues (F44E, F44D) and aromatic residues (F44Y, F44W) remarkably changed the ATP-evoked response (Figure 7E).

claim: F44E, F44D, F44Y, and F44W mutants still opened upon the application of ATP, but current decay in the continuous presence of ATP appeared to be faster than wildtype.
source: All four mutants still opened upon the application of ATP, but current decay in the continuous presence of ATP appeared to be faster than wildtype.

claim: F44 is conserved only in P2X2 and P2X3, within the P2X family.
source: F44 is conserved only in P2X2 and P2X3, within the P2X family.

claim: Other subtypes of P2X receptor, such as P2X1, P2X4, P2X6, and P2X7, except P2X5, have valine at the position corresponding to F44.
source: Other subtypes of P2X receptor, such as P2X1, P2X4, P2X6, and P2X7, except P2X5, have valine at the corresponding position (Kawate et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kawate et al., 2009

claim: F44V mutant was far less sensitive to voltage than wildtype.
source: The G-V relationship of F44V in 10 μM ATP showed that this mutant was far less sensitive to voltage than wildtype (Figure 7F).

claim: The results of the mutations introduced at position F44 showed that this residue is critical for the proper ATP- and voltage-dependent gating of the P2X2 receptor.
source: Taken together, the results of the mutations introduced at position F44 showed that this residue is critical for the proper ATP- and voltage-dependent gating of the P2X2 receptor.

claim: The phenotype of F44A/A337F was similar to F44A, and the wildtype phenotype was not rescued.
source: The phenotype of F44A/A337F was similar to F44A, and the wildtype phenotype was not rescued (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1

claim: F44E/A337R double mutant showed constitutive activity, being already open before ATP application and did not show any response to ATP.
source: The F44E/A337R pair showed constitutive activity. This double mutant was already open before ATP application and did not show any response to ATP (Figure 7G).

claim: F44E/A337R mutant lacked sensitivity to voltage, with a rectified permeation property, as seen by the total lack of tail currents.
source: When voltage step pulses were applied, this mutant lacked sensitivity to voltage, with a rectified permeation property, as seen by the total lack of tail currents (Figure 7H).

claim: A337 in the TM2 domain might interact with F44 in TM1 to stabilize the open state of the P2X2 receptor.
source: The results showed that A337 in the TM2 domain might interact with F44 in TM1 to stabilize the open state of the P2X2 receptor.
evidence: Conclusion from artificial electrostatic bridge experiments

claim: F44 moves into close proximity to the converged electric field at A337 and I341 in the presence of ATP.
source: Based on the results from VCF recording, mutagenesis experiments, and the homology modeling of rP2X2 in the open state upon ATP binding, it was shown that F44 moves into close proximity to the converged electric field at A337 and I341 (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: Conclusion from VCF, mutagenesis, and modeling, shown in Figure 8

claim: In the presence of ATP, voltage-dependent conformational changes occur, possibly at or around the position of A337 and F44.
source: In the presence of ATP, voltage-dependent conformational changes occur, possibly at or around the position of A337 and F44, giving influence to the interaction between A337 and F44, which is critical for stabilizing the open state.

claim: The origin of the voltage-dependent gating of P2X2 in the presence of ATP is possibly the voltage dependence of the interaction between A337 and F44 within the converged electric field.
source: Results of this study show that the origin of the voltage-dependent gating of P2X2 in the presence of ATP is possibly the voltage dependence of the interaction between A337 and F44 within the converged electric field (Figure 8).
evidence: Conclusion from the study, illustrated in Figure 8

claim: Electrochromic effect is a shift in the fluorophore emission spectrum due to the interaction between the fluorophore electronic state and the local electric field.
source: Electrochromic effect is a shift in the fluorophore emission spectrum due to the interaction between two components: the fluorophore electronic state and the local electric field (Bublitz and Boxer, 1997; Klymchenko and Demchenko, 2002; Dekel et al., 2012).

claim: Electrochromic effect has two distinctive characteristics: fast kinetics of fluorescent change (ΔFFast) and linear voltage dependence of the F-V relationship.
source: It has two distinctive characteristics: (1) fast kinetics of fluorescent change (ΔFFast); (2) linear voltage dependence of the F-V relationship (Asamoah et al., 2003; Klymchenko et al., 2006).

claim: If the fluorophore is directly attached in a site-specific manner within ion channels/receptors, the detection of electrochromic effect implies that there is a convergence of the electric field at the position where the fluorophore is attached.
source: If the fluorophore is directly attached in a site-specific manner within ion channels/receptors as shown by studies in the Shaker B K+ channel (Asamoah et al., 2003) and M2 muscarinic receptor (Dekel et al., 2012), the detection of electrochromic effect implies that there is a convergence of the electric field at the position where the fluorophore is attached.
evidence: Supported by citations to studies on Shaker K+ channel and M2 muscarinic receptor

claim: The observed fluorescence change at the position of A337 in the P2X2 receptor was explained to be due to the electrochromic effect, indicating that there is a focused electric field at A337 in the TM2 domain.
source: Thus, the observed fluorescence change at the position of A337 in the P2X2 receptor was explained to be due to the electrochromic effect, indicating that there is a focused electric field at A337 in the TM2 domain.
evidence: Interpretation of experimental observations based on electrochromic effect principles

claim: The most straightforward explanation to interpret the results observed in this study is that the very fast and linearly voltage-dependent fluorescence changes of Anap at A337 and I341 are associated not with the conformational changes of the P2X2 protein but presumably with the electrochromic signal.
source: Even though other possibilities still remain, the most straightforward explanation to interpret the results observed in this study is that the very fast and linearly voltage-dependent fluorescence changes of Anap at A337 and I341 are associated not with the conformational changes of the P2X2 protein but presumably with the electrochromic signal.

claim: A337 Cys mutants were not modified by MTSET both in the presence or absence of ATP.
source: A337 Cys mutants were first reported to be not modified by MTSET both in the presence or absence of ATP, indicating that this residue is not involved either in the pore lining region in the open state or in the gate of P2X2, unlike I341 Cys mutants, which were modified by MTSET (Li et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2008

claim: A337C was modified by Ag+ both in the absence and presence of ATP.
source: Meanwhile in another study using Ag+, a smaller thiol-reactive ion with higher accessibility, A337C was modified both in the absence and presence of ATP, as well as I341C (Li et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2010

claim: A narrow water phase penetrates down to the positions of A337 and I341.
source: These results suggest that a narrow water phase penetrates down to these positions, which is consistent with the results in this study that there is a focused electric field at the position of A337 and I341.

claim: TM1 plays a role in the binding-gating process, as mutations in this region alter the agonist selectivity and sensitivity of channel gating.
source: TM1 is shown to play a role in the binding-gating process, as mutations in this region alter the agonist selectivity and sensitivity of channel gating (Haines et al., 2001; Li et al., 2004; Stelmashenko et al., 2014).

claim: TM2 plays an essential role in permeation and gating.
source: In contrast, TM2 plays an essential role in permeation (Nakazawa et al., 1998; Khakh and Egan, 2005) and gating (Li et al., 2008).

claim: F44 possibly serves as a voltage sensor which has quadrupole moment due to its benzene ring.
source: Taken together, the results raised the possibility that F44 serves as a voltage sensor which has quadrupole moment due to its benzene ring (Dougherty, 1996).
evidence: Speculation based on experimental results and citation to Dougherty, 1996

claim: The aromatic side chain of F44 could have a permanent and non-spherical charge distribution that is expected to respond to voltage changes in the converged electric field.
source: The aromatic side chain of F44 could have a permanent and non-spherical charge distribution (Dougherty, 1996) that is expected to respond to voltage changes in the converged electric field.
evidence: Speculation based on citation to Dougherty, 1996

claim: The artificial electrostatic bridge in the F44E/A337R mutant induced constitutive activity in the absence of ATP and at all recorded voltages, confirming the importance of the interaction for the maintenance of the activated state.
source: The artificial electrostatic bridge in the F44E/A337R mutant (Figure 7G-I) induced constitutive activity in the absence of ATP and at all recorded voltages, confirming the importance of the interaction for the maintenance of the activated state.

claim: F44Anap was not functional, further showing the critical role of F44.
source: The structural rearrangement at F44 is of very high interest, but F44Anap was not functional, further showing the critical role of F44.

claim: The interaction between A337 and F44 in the ATP-bound open state is under the influence of the converged electric field.
source: Based on our results, the interaction between A337 and F44 in the ATP-bound open state is under the influence of the converged electric field (Figure 8A-E)
evidence: Conclusion from experimental results, illustrated in Figure 8

claim: F44 might have a two-step voltage-dependent rearrangement after moving into the proximity of A337 upon ATP application.
source: Our interpretation, based on this study, is that F44 possibly has a two-step voltage-dependent rearrangement, after moving into the proximity of A337 upon ATP application.
evidence: Interpretation and speculation based on experimental results

claim: F44 quickly orients to A337 in the open state, which is stabilized better upon hyperpolarization.
source: (1) F44 quickly orients to A337 in the open state, which is stabilized better upon hyperpolarization.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on experimental results

claim: The stabilization upon hyperpolarization, as the consequence of F44 voltage sensing, results in secondary structural rearrangements.
source: (2) The stabilization upon hyperpolarization, as the consequence of F44 voltage sensing, results in secondary structural rearrangements.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on experimental results

claim: The slow kinetics of fluorescence signal change at A337 might be the result of the second step of the voltage sensing mechanism by F44.
source: The slow kinetics of fluorescence signal change at A337 (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 2, Figure 6) might be the result of the second step of the voltage sensing mechanism by F44.
